newsitem.title: USA: CME July pork bellies close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: CME July pork bellies close sharply higher.

text.p: A last-minute buying rush boosted CME July pork bellies to a sharply higher close at 93.40 cents per lb and other contracts finished higher to up the 3.00 cent daily limit, traders said.

Two cash-connected firms led buying in July pork bellies late in the session, and gains from that action attracted local and technically-motivated buying, sources said. Chart-based buy stops were triggered near 92.50 cents and again at 93.00 in the July, they said.
A surprising reduction in U.S. frozen pork belly supplies in April fueled buying from the start and the uptrend gained momentum as prices sped through technical resistance points.

The USDA monthly Cold Storage report released late Tuesday showed a decline in supplies during April for only the second time on record, traders said. The report showed that as of U.S. May 1 frozen belly stocks were 54.017 million lbs versus 54.767 million April 1 and 57.174 million May 1 of last year.
CME pork bellies closed up 1.40 to 3.00 cents with July up 2.850 cents at 93.400. The March 1998 contract closed up the 3.00 cent limit at 76.500.
